source.note: Bounded critical treatment of the unnumbered coda of selected Charles1906 printed unit7/PDF52, existing POB6:8 editorial address. Exact selected source text, pages and English are unchanged from the original author packet. Root personally viewed actual Charles52 coda, Dillmann1865 column104 and columns959–960 after exposure to that packet and the independent adverse8finding. Column104 explicitly cites Hen6,8 in its headship entry and prints the construct ሐበይተ; selected Charles has initial ሀ in ሀበይተ. The initial-letter distinction is retained and not certified away. English chiefs is a qualified old lexical identification, not a claim of an exact same-spelling dictionary headword or manuscript uniformity. No Greek or1851reading adopted, no fresh manuscript or human-specialist certification; distinct exact critical-treatment review still required.

translation.text: These were their chiefs of tens.[a]

footnotes.text: This is the unnumbered closing coda of Charles1906 printed unit7, assigned the existing POB address6:8 by a separately reviewed editorial split; the edition prints no numeral8 here. “Chiefs” is a qualified lexical interpretation: Dillmann1865 column104 explicitly cites Hen6:8 under a headship/nobility entry and prints the construct ሐበይተ, whereas the selected Charles word has initial ሀ, ሀበይተ. That spelling difference remains unresolved, and the source is not normalized to the dictionary form or certified as a uniform manuscript reading. “Of tens” retains the numerical grouping (Dillmann959–960), without inventing a twenty-name roster. The address map alone does not approve the wording.
